references.text: God's promise to Abraham that those who bless him will be blessed, and those who curse him will be cursed. Balak seeks out Bileam to curse Israel, who are the descendants of Abraham.
Isaac's blessing over Jacob contains similar wording: those who curse shall be cursed, and those who bless shall be blessed.
Bileam explains that he was brought from Aram to curse Israel, but he cannot curse anyone whom God has not cursed.
Bileam pronounces a blessing on Israel that reflects the promise to Abraham: 'Velsignet være den som velsigner deg, forbannet være den som forbanner deg.'
Moses reminds Israel that God turned Bileam's curse into a blessing.
Joshua reminds the people how Balak sent for Bileam to curse Israel, but God refused to listen to Bileam and turned the curse into a blessing.
Nehemiah refers to the event where Balak hired Bileam to curse Israel, but God turned the curse into a blessing.
